name: Question 2
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=25x(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1,2}=\pm 5\text{i},$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1,2}=[\pm \text{i},5]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t) \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5t) \\ 5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5t)\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

For example, when ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=0,$ we obtain the following curve:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x={{field-1}} \\ y={{field-2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the coordinates (rounded to two decimal places) of several points on the curve, we get the table below.

| $t$ | $0$ | $\frac{\pi }{20}$ | $\frac{\pi }{10}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $-0.71$ | {{field-3}} |
| $y$ | $5$ | $3.54$ | {{field-4}} |
